definition: Microbes that cause disease. Twenty seconds of soap and water shifts most of them.
The grand finale of labour, usually with a midwife close at hand. "Any minute now" is rarely accurate.
A viral illness in young children with a barking, seal-like cough.
Long bouts of crying in a healthy young baby. It settles by about 3 to 4 months.
A fatty plaque in an artery wall, behind most heart attacks and strokes when it narrows or ruptures. Heart disease is a leading killer of Australian women too. Wear Red Day.
Tiny hair-like projections that sweep mucus out of the airways.
Old name for xylene, the solvent that clears tissue before wax embedding in histopathology. If you guessed this in one, please step away from the lab.
A check of care against a standard, repeated after changes to see if things improved.
The part of the body between the neck and the belly, holding the heart and lungs.
Thin woven fabric used for dressings.
An autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints and kidneys. Its name is Latin for wolf.
Sideways curve of the spine, often first noticed in the teens as one shoulder or hip sitting higher. Most cases are mild and just need watching.
Ankle bone that links the leg to the foot.
Archaic term for itchy skin disease, used for scabies and psoriasis alike. From the days when "it's itchy" counted as a diagnosis.
The hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm. The ‘funny bone’ is really the ulnar nerve.
The digit with two bones that lets us grip. It has its own big patch of brain.
Relating to the nose.
Relating to the eye or vision, as in the optic nerve.
Inflamed lining around the lungs: a sharp chest pain that’s worse with each breath or cough. Usually follows a virus, but a clot in the lung can mimic it, so get checked.
Old unit of radioactivity, named after Marie and Pierre Curie.
The large flat pelvic bone. Spelled with an ‘i’; the ileum is the gut.
The joint between the forearm and the hand, built from eight small carpal bones.
Where digestion starts. Saliva begins breaking down starch straight away.
A fist-sized pump that beats about 100,000 times a day.
One of two organs that release eggs and make oestrogen and progesterone.
A vaccine-preventable throat infection that forms a grey membrane and makes a toxin that can damage the heart. Note the PHTH: it’s the spelling most people miss.
The last part of the small intestine, where vitamin B12 is absorbed.
The hollow inside of a tube, like a blood vessel or bowel.
